The fixture also marks Valverde’s return to the Uruguay squad after missing the previous international break. item.title: Elmira Notre Dame soccer star Young makes Hofstra commitment official
item.description: There was no school for Elmira Notre Dame on Wednesday, Nov. 11 in honor of Veterans Day, but for Crusaders senior MK Young the day marked one of her most significant there. Young was joined by her coach, school staff, family, friends, and teammates for a ceremony at the Notre Dame gymnasium after officially signing her National Letter of Intent earlier in the day to play Division I women's soccer at Hofstra University on Long Island. Wednesday was the start of the early signing window for high school seniors committing to colleges in soccer and most other sports. Young's verbal commitment had been in place since last year. "I was a little bit nervous at first, but once I got up there I was just really excited to finally make it official," said Young, whose full name is Mary Katherine. "I've been waiting for this moment so long. It's nice that it's finally happening." Young recently completed one of the most prolific careers, and seasons, in Section 4 history. She finished with 124 varsity goals at Notre Dame. That included 38 goals and two assists in only 13 games this season while being the center of attention for opponents trying to keep Notre Dame from scoring. Young said she knew Hofstra was the school for her when she made her official visit, adding she got along well with the players there and liked the coaching staff. Hofstra is a member of the Coastal Athletic Association and recently finished a 6-7-5 season. More: MK Young's legacy at Notre Dame defined by goals, wins, and leadership Despite her offensive skills, Young is headed to Hofstra as an outside back or center back. Defender is the position she plays on her Syracuse Development Academy team, which gets its season going in December. "I'm very excited. I'm just very grateful for the opportunity," Young said of playing Division I soccer. She said she's looking forward to essentially starting from scratch as a college player following a Notre Dame varsity career that started in seventh grade and featured two Section 4 championships. "I feel like working my way up was so fun. It’s exciting to start over again and do it all over again," Young said. In the meantime, Young will compete in track & field for the first time, starting this winter with Notre Dame's indoor team and continuing with the spring outdoor season. She is planning to compete in sprints and relays, adding running every day will have the additional benefit of helping with soccer conditioning. Young added she is looking forward to competing in the Interscholastic Athletic Conference in track while getting more time with friends and teammates, which factored into her decision to try track. "I've never done anything like it, so I'm excited for a new experience," she said. Young lives in West Elmira with her dad, Brent Young, and younger siblings Liz and Jake. item.title: Vonn undergoes surgery to remove screws and plates from her leg
item.description: FILE PHOTO - American alpine ski racer Lindsey Vonn answers questions from media representatives at a press conference in the run-up to the Alpine World Ski Championships. (is associated with: «Vonn undergoes surgery to remove screws and plates from her leg») Jens Büttner/dpa Alpine skiing star Lindsey Vonn has successfully undergone a ninth surgery following her horrific crash at this year's Winter Olympics in Milan and Cortina d'Ampezzo. "Surgery went well. Will give you an update soon," US skier Vonn said on Instagram on Wednesday evening. She also shared a picture of a stack of screws and plates removed from her leg during the surgery. "Got all the s**t out of my leg," she wrote. In a video shared ahead of the procedure, Vonn explained that the removal of the hardware would allow surgeons to essentially build her a new ACL, having not had one since the initial rupture, which happened in a training incident before the Milano-Cortina crash. The 2010 downhill Olympic gold medallist came out of retirement in the 2024-25 with the aim of winning another Olympic medal and arrived in Italy as downhill World Cup leader. She competed in Cortina d'Ampezzo with a left knee cruciate ligament tear she sustained nine days earlier. Her Olympic race on Ferbuary 8 lasted only 13 seconds until she clipped a gate and fell heavily. She suffered a complex tibia fracture and said doctors saved her leg from an amputation.

item.description: Sundays with Papa. That’s what changed the course of Lauren Tolliver’s athletic career. The St. Mary Catholic Central student grew up as a volleyball player, but started playing golf with her grandfather, Jerry Marcero, the summer before her freshman year. “I learned from my Papa,” Tolliver said. “We would go out every Sunday (to Sandy Creek Golf Course). He was a really big into it. He used to be the manager out there for a long time.” On those lazy Sunday afternoons, Tolliver got to spend quality time with her grandpa and learn about golf. “He taught me lot about the mental part of it – how to be able to stay positive,” she said. “It was really uplifting.” Tolliver put those lessons to good work during her senior season at SMCC. She showed amazing consistency with every 9-hole round between 42 and 46 and all but two 18-hole rounds between 85 and 88. She was the medalist at the Huron League finals, third in her regional and helped the Kestrels win the Monroe County Championship and the Huron League, tie for first in regionals and place 10th in the state. She has been selected Monroe County Region Girls Golfer of the Year by The Monroe News. “After my freshman year, I just loved golf so much,” she said. “I started play all the time and indoor in the winter. My game improved so much.” Thanks to Papa, her greatest improvement came on the mental side. “You’re going to have bad shots and bad holes,” she said. “What makes golfers great is making great recoveries.” Tolliver showed her ability to do that during a key dual meet against Grosse Ile. “I hit my driver into the water,” she recalled. “When I came out, I hit a tree.” Undaunted by the misfortune, Tolliver pulled out her wedge and chipped in from 120 yards out for a birdie. “I just try to stay calm,” she said. “I don’t even check scores throughout the match. I just make sure to focus on one shot at time. Yeah, I like to celebrate good shots, but don’t get too down about bad ones.” Tolliver also is the starting shortstop for SMCC’s softball team. item.title: Longtime Rutgers football player 'elated' Greg Schiano returning in 2027
item.description: PISCATAWAY – In the transfer portal era where player movement is at an all-time high, it’s rare for a player to stick with one program their entire college career. Rutgers football defensive lineman DJ Allen is one of those exceptions. The 6-foot-7, 275-pound Allen joined the program as part of the 2022 recruiting class, meaning he was one of the earliest recruits that coach Greg Schiano brought into the program. For that reason, Schiano means a lot to Allen, who had an offer list that included Michigan, Iowa, Michigan State, Nebraska and others. Allen, an Indiana native, has been with the Scarlet Knights for now five seasons, seeing the program go through plenty of ups and downs, including this season’s 2-7 output through the first nine games – Rutgers plays Nebraska on Nov. 14 at SHI Stadium. But Allen was glad to hear he’ll be able to continue to play for Schiano next season, which became official on Nov. 10 when athletic director Keli Zinn announced Schiano would return in 2027. “We’re super exited,” Allen said following practice on Wednesday, Nov. 11. “I’ve been here for five years, and the reason why I’m here is because of Coach Schiano. Hearing that news I was elated. I’m excited to see what we’re capable of doing.” Allen said he’s confident in the program’s direction under his head coach. “I’m excited because of what he’s built here,” Allen said. “You look at his track record, he’s done great things here. I have full confidence and belief in Coach Schiano, what he’s bringing to us and what we’re going to continue to do.” It’s been a rough season for Rutgers in many ways, and the team now has three games remaining with no chance of securing the six-win mark for traditional bowl eligibility. As disappointing as it’s been, Allen echoed a message Schiano has conveyed several times this season – the team is only focusing on trying to win now, not on what’s already happened. “It’s frustrating, but I think the biggest thing is we’re focused on this week and what we can do now,” Allen said. “We can’t focus on the past. Being prepared for Nebraska is our biggest task right now.” This article originally appeared on Asbury Park Press: Longtime Rutgers football player 'elated' Greg Schiano returning in 2027

item.title: Cortaca Jug rivalry returns to Yankee Stadium. What to know
item.description: For the second time in four years, one of college football's biggest rivalries will be played at one of pro sports' most recognizable venues. Unbeaten SUNY Cortland will face Route 13 rival Ithaca College in the annual Cortaca Jug game at 1 p.m. Saturday, Nov. 14 at Yankee Stadium in the Bronx. Cortland, three years removed from a national championship, brings a 9-0 record into the contest and is ranked ninth in Division III by D3football.com and 10th by the American Football Coaches Association. The Red Dragons finished with a 7-0 record in Empire 8 play with last week's 42-24 victory over SUNY Brockport, securing an automatic berth into the NCAA Division III Tournament while extending their conference winning streak to 40 games. Ithaca is 7-2 and comes off a 14-10 loss to Rensselaer Polytechnic Institute in a game that decided the Liberty League title. The Bombers' seven-game winning streak came to a close and they ended up 6-1 in league play. This regular-season finale will be the third meeting between the teams in the New York City area. Ithaca beat Cortland, 32-20, in front of an announced Division III record crowd of 45,161 fans at MetLife Stadium in East Rutherford, New Jersey in 2019. In 2022, Ithaca beat Cortland, 34-17, in front of 40,232 fans at Yankee Stadium. "Cortland and Ithaca both help set the standard in Division III athletics, and our Cortaca Jug rivalry demonstrates that shared excellence," Mike Urtz, Cortland's athletic director, said in a press release when it was announced the rivalry would return to Yankee Stadium. "It's been called the 'biggest little game in the nation' for a reason, and it's fitting to be played in one of the most iconic sports venues in the entire world." Ithaca won last year's meeting, 26-21, at home. This will be the 67th Cortaca Jug game and the 84th all-time meeting between the schools. Ithaca leads the series 44-36-3. The Cortaca Jug made its debut in 1959, the first Cortaca Jug game. There are now three Cortaca Jugs after the first two ran out of space to chronicle scores. item.description: ST. CLOUD — After a 0-1-1 weekend in Omaha and a bye week for the No. 9 women's team, both Husky hockey squads are back in action this weekend against powerful in-state foes. The men host No. 8 Minnesota Duluth, and the women make the quick trek to No. 2 Minnesota as the two teams stand on opposite sides of the spectrum with conference play ramping up. The men drop the puck at 7 p.m., Friday, Nov. 13 and at 6 p.m., Saturday, Nov. 14 against Duluth; both games will be available on the Twin Cities CW and can be heard over radio at KNSI (1450 AM/99.3 FM). The women's team starts at 6 p.m., Friday, Nov. 13 and at 1 p.m., Saturday, Nov. 14; both games can be streamed on B1G+. Over on the men's side of things, the Huskies are a disappointing but competitive 3-5-1 through the early portion of the season, with three one-goal defeats and two strong wins against No. 14 Michigan Tech and Boston College. They once again showed those flashes of excellence against the Mavericks, but failed to put together a full 60-minute effort to secure a win. item.description: James Anderson made his Lancashire debut in 2001 [Getty Images] Legendary England bowler James Anderson has extended his record-breaking career beyond his 45th birthday by signing for Surrey. England's all-time leading Test wicket-taker was not offered a new contract by Lancashire, the county for whom he first played professionally 25 years ago. Amid interest from multiple clubs, the 44-year-old has agreed a move to The Oval and could play on beyond the 2027 season. Speaking on a special episode of his Tailenders podcast, Anderson said: "I'm just incredibly excited. "Going from thinking I might not play cricket again to having this opportunity - I'm properly buzzing for it. "I'm not doing this for a send-off. That's not the reason I've signed for Surrey." Referring to his exit from Lancashire last month, Anderson said: "There was a bit of emotion in that few days. "I was really conscious on not making a decision based on that emotion, so that's why I have taken a few weeks to try to get my ahead around everything and decide what the best way forward is. "Finding a club that wants me and has that same motivation to win trophies - I just want to be a part of something." The move to Surrey is another – probably final – chapter in Anderson's remarkable career. He will turn 45 in July. After taking 704 wickets in 188 matches, Anderson sits third on the all-time list of Test bowlers, with more scalps than any other seamer. His 911 international wickets is also an England record and a record for all pace bowlers. Anderson was forced into international retirement by England in the summer of 2024, then returned to play for Lancashire for two seasons, captaining them this summer. Although Anderson claimed 50 wickets, Lancashire finished second bottom of Division Two of the County Championship. New Lancashire director of cricket Paul Farbrace took the decision to release Anderson as part of a "rebuild" of the squad. In leaving Old Trafford, Anderson has departed a ground which has an end named after him. Now Anderson links up with Surrey after talks with director of cricket Alec Stewart, who was in the England team when the seamer made his international debut in 2002. Anderson has signed a red-ball only deal, although Anderson he said he would play white-ball cricket if required. There is no official coaching element to the contract. Anderson has not decided if he will relocate his family – his wife and two daughters – from their home in Cheshire. "After thinking what would be best for me, what's best for my family and where I want to play, it was a fairly easy decision," said Anderson. "I did feel like I wanted to play again after having a good year last year. I don't feel like I'm done yet. I feel like I've got more to offer on the field. "Surrey is such a strong squad, challenging for the Championship. It's the chance to play in Division One again, which I haven't done for a few years. I just thought it was a really exciting challenge to try to take on.

item.title: Zeeland water polo has stepped up in every big moment, the next could be a state title
item.description: ZEELAND - The Zeeland boys water polo team knew the state meet would be in its home pool. In response, the team won a conference title and regional crown for the first time since 2008 and earned the state's No. 1 ranking for the first time. Zeeland enters the state tournament as the top seed and hosts Mason at 10:30 p.m. Friday, Nov. 13. It took two one-goal wins to earn the regional title. In past years, Zeeland has not always excelled in those pivotal moments. This year's group is different. More: How a stunning pool-length goal led Zeeland to a historic regional water polo title More: Zeeland water polo earns historic No. 1 ranking, defense leading team toward state title The team has won several one-goal games and a few in the final seconds. "It is just about having the confidence to do it," Zeeland coach Zac Geschwendt said. "They know they have been in that situation more times than they haven't. We have come up with some spectacular wins this season." In the regional semifinals, Andrew Pyle scored a goal that traveled three quarters of the length of the pool and went in with one second remaining. Pyle also scored a goal from the midpoint of the pool in the final seconds to beat Rockford. "It started at the West Ottawa tournament when we were down six to Rockford and came racing back before Pyle hit the half-court winner with 3 seconds left," Geschwendt said. "Since then, we have had a lot of close games the we have won. The more those happened, the more confidence we built." And that has turned into a special season. "It has been really great coming out senior year and having one of our best seasons in school history. I think we have a really good shot at the state title this year, and I am really excited for it," Carson Durham said. While Pyle is an all-state player, and has been, the team doesn't rely on just him. Just about every player on the roster has scored a game-winning goal or made a game-saving block. "It is a new person each game, which is really cool," Durham said. And the next moments will be at the Zeeland Natatorium. And who will be the hero? "It has been a big drive for the team to perform well this season, having it at home," Andrew Skaggs said. "We know our teammates have our back and that builds trust." item.description: Tim Sherwood makes stunning Harry Kane to Man United claim amid Pochettino arrival Former Premier League manager Tim Sherwood has sensationally tipped Harry Kane to reunite with Mauricio Pochettino at Manchester United. item.title: “I’m sometimes surprised” Zubimendi responds to Atletico Madrid rumours
item.description: “I’m sometimes surprised” Zubimendi responds to Atletico Madrid rumours Martin Zubimendi has been linked with a move away from Arsenal in recent months , despite insisting that he remains committed to the club. The midfielder has found regular game time difficult to secure since arriving at the Emirates, leading to speculation about his future. Arsenal were keen to strengthen their squad across all competitions during the last transfer window and added quality to a midfield that had already helped them win the league. Myles Lewis-Skelly has also emerged as a solid option in that area, giving Mikel Arteta further choices. As a result, Zubimendi has spent much of the current campaign in the unfamiliar position of a substitute. Neither the player nor Arteta is accustomed to that situation, but the manager has continued to make his selection decisions with the team’s needs in mind. Atletico Madrid linked with January move Players of Zubimendi’s quality naturally want to play regularly, and reports suggest that he could leave Arsenal just 18 months after joining the Gunners. Atletico Madrid have reportedly moved close to signing the midfielder in January, raising further questions about his long-term future in north London. The Spaniard spent most of his career in his home country before making the move to Arsenal . A return to Spain could therefore be an option, particularly if he continues to struggle for regular opportunities under Arteta. However, the midfielder has now addressed the speculation and made it clear that he is not close to leaving the Premier League club. He also expressed surprise at some of the reports circulating about his future. (Photo by Mike Hewitt/Getty Images) Zubimendi responds to transfer rumours Speaking to Marca , Zubimendi questioned the accuracy of the stories linking him with a move and called for greater care when reporting on transfer speculation. “To be honest, I’m sometimes surprised by the press too. I understand that the winter transfer window is approaching and rumors can surface, but I think we need to be a bit more careful with what we publish. Ultimately, everyone has a team they play for, and we need to respect that. I’ve also read that I might be close, but not at all.” His comments offer a clear response to the reports suggesting that Atletico Madrid are close to securing his signature. item.title: Pau Cubarsi and Gerard Martin share a remarkable injury record under Hansi Flick
item.description: Pau Cubarsi and Gerard Martin share a remarkable injury record under Hansi Flick Barcelona’s injury problems under Hansi Flick have made squad availability an increasingly important part of the German manager’s work. However, a report from SPORT has highlighted two notable exceptions, namely Pau Cubarsi and Gerard Martin, who are the only two outfield players among 23 footballers to have avoided missing a Barcelona match through injury since the beginning of Flick’s tenure in 2024/25. While several established players, including Lamine Yamal, Raphinha and Pedri, have struggled with recurring physical problems, the two defenders have maintained their availability, providing Flick with unusual continuity in a defence that has frequently required adjustments. Cubarsi and Gerard Martin provide rare injury consistency Notably, Cubarsi has featured in 117 matches since the beginning of the 2024/25 season, missing just 16 fixtures. Importantly, two of those absences were caused by suspension rather than injury. Interestingly, even an ankle problem suffered while representing Spain in March 2025 failed to keep him out of Barcelona’s matches. Pau Cubarsi and Gerard Martin have never missed a game through injury for Flick. (Photo by Dan Mullan/Getty Images) Gerard Martin, on his part, has also maintained an impressive record, participating in 107 matches during the same period. He has missed 25 fixtures, all through the manager’s selection decisions rather than physical problems. The left-footed defender did suffer a metacarpal fracture, but the injury occurred after the season had concluded and therefore did not affect his availability for Barcelona. Szczesny’s record comes with an important qualification Notably, Wojciech Szczesny can technically be included among Barcelona’s injury-free players since joining the club in October 2024. However, his situation is different because he has made only 43 appearances. Szczesny has also been fit, although he picked up the flu. (Photo by Alex Caparros/Getty Images) The Polish goalkeeper also missed a Barcelona fixture because of gastroenteritis, meaning his record of avoiding injuries does not represent uninterrupted availability for selection. Nevertheless, Cubarsi and Gerard Martin stand out because their records have been maintained despite considerably greater involvement on the pitch. Christensen shows the other side of Barcelona’s injury problems At the same time, Andreas Christensen sits on the other side of the spectrum. The Danish defender, who recently returned from injury , has accumulated 433 days on the sidelines through injuries, equivalent to more than a year away from competitive football. Understandably, his prolonged absences have deprived Flick of a reliable defensive option and prevented him from establishing consistent involvement in the team, which was one of the reasons why Gerard Martin was moved into the centre-back role from his usual left-back position.

item.title: Carlo Ancelotti hands Brazil captaincy to Barcelona forward Raphinha ahead of Vinicius Jr and Bruno Guimaraes for Japan and Singapore friendlies
item.description: Brazil v Uruguay - FIFA World Cup 2026 Qualifier - Getty Images Sport Brazil head coach Carlo Ancelotti has selected Barcelona forward Raphinha to wear the captain's armband for Saturday's international friendly against Japan in Singapore. The 29-year-old was chosen ahead of Vinicius Jr and Bruno Guimaraes after regular skipper Marquinhos missed out through injury. Catalan star assumes leadership role According to MARCA , Ancelotti has entrusted Raphinha with leading the Selecao out at the Singapore National Stadium after Paris Saint-Germain defender Marquinhos suffered a muscular injury against the Catalan giants in the Champions League. Although not his first time skippering the side, the call-up rewards the attacker's growing influence at club and international level. Recent training sessions indicate he will start Saturday's fixture on November 14. Established hierarchy guides armband decision With his primary leader unavailable, the former Real Madrid boss and his coaching staff weighed up several alternatives, including Gabriel Magalhaes alongside Guimaraes and Vinicius. While rotating the armband across the squad was also considered, the Italian tactician ultimately opted to preserve the pecking order established during the previous international window. The Spanish publication notes that Newcastle United midfielder Guimaraes sits next in line and will assume the duties whenever the Blaugrana winger is off the pitch. Rewarding the forward reflects his status as a senior dressing-room figure under Hansi Flick in Spain, where he has already netted 19 goals across all competitions this term despite fitness setbacks. Club officials monitor international workload Because the wide man picked up a knock during the last international break, chiefs in Catalonia will closely track his minutes over the coming days. Initial plans suggest that while the newly installed skipper will feature from the outset, he is unlikely to complete the full 90 minutes in either match to manage his workload. This November trip marks the third time the South Americans have visited the Asian nation following previous stops in 2014 and 2019 at the 55,000-capacity venue, which opened on June 30, 2014. During their first visit under Dunga on October 14, 2014, shortly after beating Argentina 2-1 in Beijing, Neymar scored all four goals in a 4-0 rout of the Blue Samurai before Roberto Firmino and Casemiro netted in consecutive 1-1 draws against Senegal and Nigeria five years later. Asian tour concludes calendar year Following Saturday's meeting with the Japanese, Brazil wrap up their 2026 schedule at the same arena against hosts Singapore on Tuesday, November 17. Paraguay are also participating in the four-team series, facing the home nation on Friday before taking on the Blue Samurai next Tuesday. Returning to Spain unscathed will be vital for Raphinha as Flick's side resume their domestic and European campaigns later this month.

item.description: Steph Curry left Rockets game with an injury © X/ @warriors The Golden State Warriors suffered a major blow on Wednesday when Steph Curry left the game against the Houston Rockets with an injury. item.title: World Cup boss ready to replace Michael Carrick at Manchester United
item.description: World Cup boss ready to replace Michael Carrick at Manchester United Mauricio Pochettino to Manchester United: Carrick Decision Nears as Talks AdvanceOK Manchester United look to be moving towards another managerial change, and this time the picture is unusually clear. According to BBC Sport, Mauricio Pochettino is prepared to step in if the call comes, with Michael Carrick now appearing to be on borrowed time at Old Trafford. The key line is simple and significant: “Mauricio Pochettino is ready to accept an offer from Manchester United to become their next head coach.” That tells you plenty. There is no dancing around it, no vague briefing, no polite distancing. If United decide to move, the man they want is open to taking it. United have already “opened talks with the Argentine about him potentially replacing Michael Carrick”, and that alone says Carrick’s position is effectively hanging by a thread. Clubs do not hold serious conversations with a replacement unless they are well down the road of deciding the current man is done. Photo: IMAGO Pochettino talks show Manchester United intent Pochettino currently manages the United States national team, but the report states that “sources have told BBC Sport that USA manager Pochettino wants to take the job.” Again, this is not complicated. He sees Manchester United as a major opening and, by the sounds of it, one worth leaving an international post for after only a short time in charge. There is a financial element too. United would need to pay “$10m (£7.5m) to release Pochettino from his contract”, a fee that is notable but hardly prohibitive for a club of this size. If United believe he is the right fit, that number will not be the obstacle. The report also notes that “US Soccer officials are expecting an official approach from United” and already have “a contingency plan for their manager leaving, which includes a succession plan.” That matters. It suggests this is not speculative noise. People on the American side are preparing for the possibility that Pochettino goes. There is a practical issue around timing. The USA have a two-legged Concacaf Nations League quarter-final against Haiti, but the report says that, with the succession planning in place, “it raises the possibility that Pochettino may not take charge of those games.” In other words, if United accelerate, this could move quickly. Michael Carrick under pressure after dreadful start This is the backdrop that has forced United into action. They are 18th in the Premier League, in the relegation zone, after one win in ten and no victories since August. The article points out that “It is the club’s lowest position at this stage of a top-flight season since 1986-87, when they were 20th.” For Manchester United, that is beyond poor. It is a crisis by any sensible standard. Carrick’s future is expected to be decided at a meeting in Monaco involving chief executive Omar Berrada, director of football Jason Wilcox and co-owner Sir Jim Ratcliffe.

item.title: Rob Gronkowski says the Las Vegas Raiders made one of the best moves in NFL history
item.description: Photo by Michael Owens/Getty Images There is rarely a “win-win” trade in the NFL, but Rob Gronkowski thinks that the Las Vegas Raiders just made one of the best moves in NFL history. The NFL landscape changed recently when Kirk Cousins was traded by the Las Vegas Raiders to the Minnesota Vikings. Cousins returns to familiar surroundings, having played for the Vikings between 2018 to 2023, while the Raiders get good value for a player they signed for cheap. Rob Gronkowski believes that the trade is win-win, but the Raiders have actually made one of the best moves in NFL history. Rob Gronkowski hails the Kirk Cousins trade Cousins joined the Raiders at the start of this season and through nine games, it was clear that this was not a winning team. The Raiders went 4-5 through nine games, and even though Cousins was doing well, he was one of their most tradeable assets. The team did not hesitate for one second, and flipped Cousins for good value to bring the curtains on a short but fruitful spell. Gronkowski said on The Kay Adams show : “No, I didn’t call the Kirk Cousins trade. Actually, it caught me by surprise, but let me tell you, it totally makes sense all across the board. I mean, you’ve got to give it to John Spytek, their general manager. I mean, that was one of the best usages of a quarterback in NFL history. There’s no doubt about that. “He signed Kirk Cousins to a deal, kind of a cheap deal, got the most out of him. I mean, he leads the league in touchdown passes thrown. I mean, he’s having a heck of a year, and then boom, trades him, gets value from him. A third-round pick to the Minnesota Vikings. “Let me tell you, it couldn’t have been a better fit for the Minnesota Vikings either. He’s going back to Minnesota. He knows the playbook. He knows Kevin O’Connell. He knows the offence there. He knows the fan base.” Cousins now joins 6-2 Vikings, who have strengthened their roster to improve their chances of winning, while the Raiders pivot to a reset since Cousins didn’t fit their timeline anyway. It’s a win-win trade for both teams, but considering where the Raiders were from a point of view of contending, getting Cousins off the roster is a great move. item.description: Brent Venables & Oklahoma Sooners © Instagram/@ou_football The Oklahoma Sooners’ season has been a struggle, and with the program’s playoff hopes effectively over after 10 weeks, many questions have been raised about OU coach Brent Venables’ future with the program. The news of Venables not being on the hot seat despite his disappointing season did not sit well with fans online. “Mediocrity is accepted now. Program is decaying,” a fan wrote on X. The Oklahoma Sooners’ disappointing season comes against the backdrop of the program reaching the 2025 College Football Playoff in a 10-3 season, falling in the first round to the Alabama Crimson Tide. Brent Venables’ Contract Extension Details Coming off a fairly successful 2025 season, the Oklahoma Sooners gave Brent Venables a six-year contract extension before the start of this season. The six-year contract extension worth $63 million puts Venables in charge of the Sooners through the 2032 season, raking in an average salary of $10.5 million per season. If OU were to part ways with Venables, they would be liable to pay him a pricey buyout worth over $50 million. item.title: Joe Hart pinpoints ‘unbelievable’ Alisson Becker trait which makes him ‘one of the best’
item.description: Joe Hart pinpoints ‘unbelievable’ Alisson Becker trait which makes him ‘one of the best’ Joe Hart has proclaimed that Alisson Becker will ‘forever be regarded as one of the best’ goalkeepers to have graced the Premier League. Liverpool’s number 1 has been rightly acknowledged as one of the foremost players in his position in world football since his move to Anfield in 2018 and has been pivotal towards the trophies won by the Reds in that time. He produced one of his greatest LFC performances in the victory at Crystal Palace last weekend, with his tally of six saves including a world-class reaction stop from Daichi Kamada which left the Eagles attacker astounded . Hart heaps praise on ‘unbelievable’ Alisson In an interview with The Athletic , Hart lavished praise on Alisson for the consistency he’s shown throughout his time in England, and especially his prowess in one-on-saves. The ex-Manchester City stopper said of the 34-year-old: “One of the best to do it in the Premier League. What I love is his simplicity. He’s not necessarily eye-catching in the way he moves, but it’s the way he deals with everything. “He makes massive saves. His one-on-one technique is unbelievable, and he has made it his own. He very rarely gets beaten one-on-one, which in this Premier League is incredible because you’re up against some of the best strikers in the world. “He’s struggled a bit with injuries lately, but I think he’ll forever be regarded as one of the best to play the position.” (Photo by Justin Setterfield/Getty Images) Want more Empire of the Kop coverage? Add us as a preferred source on Google to your favourites list for news you can trust Alisson continues to prove he’s one of the best Last weekend, Alisson produced a perfect example of the one-on-one ability that Hart pinpointed by thwarting Yeremy Pino when the Crystal Palace forward was through on goal, a significant intervention at a time that Liverpool were 2-0 up. When it comes to ‘massive saves’, it mightn’t quite be in the same category as his legendary stoppage-time heroics against Napoli in December 2018 when our Champions League campaign was in the balance, but it showed that the 34-year-old remains a world-class goalkeeper. His outstanding display at Selhurst Park came after a couple of costly misjudgements in defeats to Arsenal and Fenerbahce, which shows the Brazilian’s strength of character to put those unfortunate moments behind him and come up trumps for his team. Alisson’s agent Ze Maria revealed in recent days that talks have begun over a prospective contract renewal at Liverpool, with the Reds’ number 1 having said after the win at Palace that he’d like to stay at Anfield beyond the expiry of his current deal next summer. More heroics like those he produced in south London four days ago, and an extension to his existing terms should be a no-brainer for sporting director Julian Ward.
